introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Philosophy (0790), Paper 2 (Philosophical Culture), P52, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: three hours.**

Candidates are expected to answer FOUR (04) questions chosen from the three sections imperatively.

Each essay must contain:
- An introduction = 5 marks
- A thesis = 7 marks
- An antithesis = 6 marks
- A synthesis = 3 marks
- A conclusion = 4 marks

Each question carries 25 marks.

Candidates are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation of material.
incertitudes: Regle de choix : la page de garde dit « answer FOUR (04) questions chosen from the three sections imperatively » (quatre questions au total, prises dans les trois sections, donc au moins une par section). `regles_choix` porte ce minimum, une regle `parmi 1 sur 2` par section (Section One : questions 1-2 ; Section Two : questions 3-4 ; Section Three : questions 5-6) ; la regle « 4 questions en tout » n'est pas exprimable en entier et est recopiee dans `introduction_markdown`. Le sujet ne dit pas explicitement « au moins une » ni si un candidat peut traiter les deux questions d'une meme section : c'est une lecture de « imperatively » et du total de quatre.

Points : chaque question est imprimee « 25 marks » (4 x 25 = 100). Les criteres de la page de garde (introduction 5, these 7, antithese 6, synthese 3, conclusion 4 = 25) s'appliquent aux dissertations (questions 1 a 4) ; les corriges des dissertations suivent ce plan et indiquent les points par partie. Questions de texte (5 et 6) : a) 2 + 3 = 5, b) 4 (2 par expression, repartition choisie par le redacteur), c) 4, d) 4, e) 4, f) 4 = 25 ; aucun ecart de somme, aucun point corrige.

Aucun corrige officiel : les corriges sont des reponses modeles redigees de memoire, sans acces a une source. Les auteurs et positions cites sont ceux de l'histoire de la philosophie etablie, sans citation litterale, sans numero de page et sans date precise hors reperes de siecle et quelques dates admises (1945 Manchester, 1957 independance du Ghana, 1963 OUA, 2002 UA) ; a faire relire par un enseignant de philosophie avant mise en avant.

Sujet scanne (3 pages) avec filigrane gcerevision.com / Kawlo sans incidence sur la lecture ; aucune figure ni tableau. Page de garde verifiee : ADVANCED LEVEL, Philosophy, « Paper 2 (Philosophical Culture) », code 0790, P52, JUNE 2026, three hours. Intitule du paper et criteres recopies tels qu'imprimes (« Philosophical Culture », « imperatively », « Candidates are expected to »).

Q1 : le corrige s'appuie sur la tradition doxographique (Aristote, Theophrastus et auteurs tardifs) pour Anaximene : air illimite, raréfaction et condensation, terre plate portee par l'air ; aucune citation litterale. L'analogie ame/air est donnee comme « rapportee ». A faire relire.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Anaximenes was preoccupied with the originating substance of the universe. Assess his theory.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction (5 marks).** The first Greek philosophers asked a question about the world as a whole: what is the one originating substance (the *arche*) from which everything comes, and by which everything is explained? Thales had answered water and Anaximander (his fellow citizen of Miletus) had answered the *apeiron*, the boundless or indefinite. Anaximenes of Miletus (6th century BC) is reported to have been Anaximander's pupil or successor. He answered that the originating substance is **air**, and he added an explanation of how one stuff can become the many things we see. We have no complete work of his, only later reports and a few fragments transmitted by Aristotle, Theophrastus and other writers, so every assessment is based on secondary sources. The problem is this: is his theory a real advance in the search for a rational account of nature, or only a change of name for a substance chosen without proof?

**Thesis: the theory is a real advance (7 marks).**
- *A definite but unlimited substance.* Air is a familiar, observable stuff, unlike Anaximander's indefinite *apeiron*, which is hard to picture and does not explain how definite qualities come out of it. Anaximenes keeps what was good in Anaximander (the principle is unlimited in extent, never exhausted and always in motion) but gives it a concrete character.
- *A mechanism of change: rarefaction and condensation.* The great merit of Anaximenes is that he explains how the one substance becomes many things. Air, when rarefied (made thinner), becomes fire; when condensed, it becomes wind, then cloud, then water, then earth and finally stones. Differences of *quality* (hot, cold, wet, solid) are thus reduced to differences of *quantity* (density). This is the first known attempt to explain qualitative variety by a quantitative process, and it anticipates the later scientific ambition to explain nature by measurable change.
- *Explanation of the weather and of the world.* The same process accounts for wind, clouds, rain, and, according to the reports, the formation of the earth, imagined as a flat body riding on the air, and of the heavenly bodies, which are made of fire. Natural events are explained by natural causes, without appeal to the will of the gods. That is the common achievement of the Milesians.
- *Life and order.* Air is also linked to breath and life. The reports say that he compared the soul, which holds us together, with the air that surrounds and holds together the whole world. Air is thus both the material and the living, ordering principle of the cosmos, so it explains motion without a separate mover.
- *Influence.* The idea of a single material principle changing by physical processes, and of a world formed by condensation and rarefaction, passed on to later thinkers, and the pre-Socratic search for the *arche* shaped the beginning of natural philosophy and science.

**Antithesis: the theory has serious limits (6 marks).**
- *The choice of air is arbitrary.* Why air rather than water or fire? Anaximenes gives no argument that air has a better claim than the others. His preference rests on observation and analogy (breath, wind, mist), not on proof.
- *Weak empirical support.* The change of air into fire, water and earth is asserted from everyday impressions, not tested. Rarefaction and condensation are not shown to produce the qualities that are said to result from them.
- *Material monism has its own difficulty.* If everything is air, how do real qualitative differences arise? Later thinkers (Parmenides on the impossibility of change, Empedocles with four elements, the Atomists with atoms and void, Anaxagoras with many seeds) judged that one changing substance cannot explain the plurality of the world.
- *Hylozoism and vagueness.* Air is said to be alive and divine, which mixes matter with life and divinity. The origin of the motion of air, and the reason why it condenses here and rarefies there, are not explained. Aristotle classes Anaximenes among those who recognised only a *material* cause, so his account misses the other causes.
- *Poor sources.* Our knowledge comes through later writers who used their own categories, so we cannot be sure of the details.

**Synthesis (3 marks).** Anaximenes' theory should be judged by its place in history rather than by its truth. As cosmology it is mistaken, and its main choice (air) is unsupported. As a method it is a step forward, because it proposes one natural principle, a natural process (rarefaction and condensation) and a quantitative way of explaining qualitative change. His merit is to have turned the intuition of Thales and the abstraction of Anaximander into a testable kind of explanation, even though he did not test it.

**Conclusion (4 marks).** Anaximenes' theory that air is the originating substance is open to the objections of arbitrariness, lack of evidence and incomplete explanation. But it deserves a positive assessment: it gave the Milesian programme a concrete principle, a natural mechanism of change and a way of connecting quality with quantity. It is therefore a significant, though imperfect, contribution to the rational explanation of the universe.
